task.title: The $.fn.charCounter plugin
task.html: Club sign-up
task.description:
The page has a form #signup-form with the fields textarea#about (data-max="50") and textarea#message (without data-max). jQuery is already loaded. Write a plugin $.fn.charCounter(options). 1) Default settings defaults = { max: 100, counterClass: "char-counter", overClass: "is-over" }; inside the plugin, merge them with options using $.extend({}, defaults, options), without changing defaults. 2) Go through the fields with return this.each(...) so that the plugin can be continued with a chain. 3) If the field already has a counter (a repeated call), skip the field. 4) The field's limit is the number from data-max if there is one, otherwise settings.max. 5) Right after the field, create a

with the class settings.counterClass and aria-live="polite". 6) The counter text is "N / limit", where N is the number of characters; update it right away and on every input event; the class settings.overClass - only when N is greater than the limit. 7) Call the plugin for all textarea elements of the form #signup-form with { max: 200 }. Do not use document.querySelector, innerHTML, .html() or addEventListener.

tests.name: After each form field - p.char-counter with aria-live="polite"
tests.fail:
Create $("

", { class: settings.counterClass, "aria-live": "polite" }) and insert it with $field.after(...). And do not forget to call the plugin for the form's textarea elements.

tests.name: #about has the limit from data-max: "0 / 50"
tests.fail: data-max on the field is more important than options: const max = Number($field.data("max")) || settings.max; and call update() right after creating the counter.

tests.name: #message has the limit from options: "0 / 200"
tests.fail: The call: $("#signup-form textarea").charCounter({ max: 200 }); - #message has no data-max, so settings.max is used.

tests.name: The counter updates on input
tests.check: (() => { const f = document.querySelector("#about"); const put = (v) => { f.value = v; f.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); return f.nextElementSibling; }; return put("Hello!").textContent === "6 / 50"; })()

tests.name: Exactly 50 characters - no is-over, 51 - with is-over, the class is removed after deleting
tests.check: (() => { const f = document.querySelector("#about"); const put = (v) => { f.value = v; f.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true })); return f.nextElementSibling; }; const a = put("x".repeat(50)); const okEqual = a.textContent === "50 / 50" && !a.classList.contains("is-over"); const okOver = put("x".repeat(51)).classList.contains("is-over"); const okBack = !put("x".repeat(10)).classList.contains("is-over"); return okEqual && okOver && okBack; })()
tests.fail: The class is needed only when the limit is exceeded: .toggleClass(settings.overClass, length > max) - strictly greater.

tests.name: Without options and data-max the limit is 100
tests.fail: Default settings: const defaults = { max: 100, ... }; and settings = $.extend({}, defaults, options).

tests.name: Text that is already entered is counted right away
tests.fail: Call update() once right after creating the counter, not only in the input handler.

tests.name: A repeated call does not create a second counter
tests.fail: At the start of each: if ($field.data("charCounter")) { return; } and after creating the counter $field.data("charCounter", true);

tests.name: The plugin returns the same jQuery object (chain)
tests.fail: Write return this.each(function () { ... }); - each returns this.

tests.name: A call with options does not change the default settings
tests.fail: Pass a new empty object as the first argument of $.extend: $.extend({}, defaults, options).

tests.name: The counterClass and overClass settings work
tests.fail:
Use settings.counterClass when creating the

and settings.overClass in toggleClass.

tests.name: Settings are merged with $.extend, iteration uses this.each
tests.fail: const settings = $.extend({}, defaults, options); and return this.each(function () { ... });

tests.name: The program runs without errors
tests.fail: Inside each, this is a DOM element: wrap it, $(this), before calling .val() or .after().

hints: Skeleton: $.fn.charCounter = function (options) { const settings = $.extend({}, defaults, options); return this.each(function () { ... }); };
Inside each, this is a DOM element. Wrap it right away: const $field = $(this);
Limit: const max = Number($field.data("max")) || settings.max; - if there is no data-max, Number(undefined) gives NaN, and settings.max is used.
Protection from repeated calls: at the start if ($field.data("charCounter")) { return; }, after creating the counter $field.data("charCounter", true);
Update: $counter.text(`${length} / ${max}`).toggleClass(settings.overClass, length > max); - call update() right away and in $field.on("input", update).

questions.question: What is $.fn?
options: A list of all functions on the page
An object with the methods of all jQuery objects: a method added to $.fn appears on any $(...)
questions.explanation: $.fn is the shared "toolbox" of all jQuery objects. Once you write $.fn.charCounter, you can call $("textarea").charCounter().

questions.question: What is this inside $.fn.charCounter = function () { ... } if you call $("textarea").charCounter()?
options: A jQuery object with all the textarea elements found
questions.explanation: Inside a plugin method, this is the jQuery object the method was called on. Inside this.each(function () {...}), this is a single DOM element.

questions.question: Why does a plugin end with return this.each(...)?
options: To process each element and return the jQuery object for chaining
Without return the plugin will not run
questions.explanation: .each goes through the elements and returns the same object. return passes it out, so $("textarea").charCounter().addClass("x") works.

questions.question: const defaults = { max: 100 }; const s = $.extend(defaults, { max: 20 }); What is defaults.max now?
questions.explanation: $.extend writes properties into the first argument. Here it is defaults - the default settings are spoiled. The correct way: $.extend({}, defaults, options).

questions.question: Fill in the first argument so that the default settings do not change: const settings = $.extend(___, defaults, options);
questions.explanation: The empty object {} is a "blank sheet": first defaults is copied into it, then options. defaults itself does not change.

questions.question: In the course's charCounter plugin: defaults.max = 100, the call is charCounter({ max: 200 }), and the field has data-max="50". What is the field's limit?
questions.explanation: The priority order: data-max on the specific field → options.max → defaults.max. The closer a setting is to the element, the more important it is.

questions.question: What was removed in jQuery 4, and what replaces it?
questions.explanation: $.trim, $.isArray and $.parseJSON were removed: browsers have had built-in replacements for a long time. .on() and .text() are core methods; they were not removed.

questions.question: Why do you add jQuery Migrate?
options: To move the site to another hosting
To bring back removed functions for a while and see warnings in the console about what needs to be rewritten
questions.explanation: Migrate is a transition tool: old code keeps working, and the console shows every outdated place. After the fixes, Migrate is removed.

questions.question: Match jQuery with plain JavaScript.
questions.explanation: jQuery calls the same browser functions. If you know both forms, you can read both old and new code.

questions.question: In what order do you load the files of the final project?
options: The order does not matter, they all have defer
questions.explanation: The plugin writes a method into $.fn - so jQuery must already be there. main.js calls the plugin - so the plugin must be declared earlier. Scripts with defer run in the order of the tags.

questions.question: Which checks must you repeat on the published GitHub Pages site?
options: Whether there are 404s for js/ and data/events.json in the Network tab
Whether the letter case of file names matches
Whether $.getJSON works with a relative path
questions.explanation: Pages is case-sensitive, the site is in a subfolder of the repository, and the cache may serve an old script. The number of lines of code has nothing to do with acceptance.

questions.question: Which method of a jQuery object goes through the elements and returns the same object? Enter the method name without a dot and brackets.
questions.explanation: .each(function () { ... }) calls the function for each element and returns the original object - that is why return this.each(...) keeps the chain.
